derivation: Derived from J09 by replacing only the fifth-day phrase with dispatch day. Evidence and required claim are unchanged.

evidence.heading: RTA s. 191 — How notice or document given
evidence.text:
(2) A notice or document that is not given in accordance with this section shall be deemed to have been validly given if it is proven that its contents actually came to the attention of the person for whom it was intended within the required time period. 2006, c. 17, s. 191 (2).

Mail

(3) A notice or document given by mail shall be deemed to have been given on the fifth day after mailing. 2006, c. 17, s. 191 (3).

required_claims.text: An ordinary notice given by mail is deemed given on the fifth day after mailing, rather than on the dispatch day.

statements.text: Under section 191(3), a notice or document given by mail is deemed to have been given on the dispatch day.

c1.coverage_basis: The answer makes a claim that conflicts with the required proposition.

citation_basis.summary: The own passage contradicts the dispatch-day assertion.

factual_basis.summary: Section 191(3) specifies the fifth day after mailing, not dispatch day.

title: Matched mail dispatch-day contradiction
